A

Austin

Beware, these are not 8.5"x11" pieces of paper

Beware, these are not full sized pieces of paper like what you would pull out of a printer. If you plan to staple these to printed paper it can be quite annoying. They are significantly smaller. The pages also rip easily if you are not careful. They feel cheap and thin. Of course these notebooks ARE cheap, so you get what you pay for. I recommend the Five-Star gridline notebooks for higher quality and a full sized piece of paper.

M

Melaina Lara

Notes a notebook

These are decent quality and a great price. For some reasfinding graph notebooks isn't as easy as running into your nearest target where lined notebooks abound.Enter this 8 pack, I received 2 each of four colors and the quality was consistent and good for all of them. The pages are not thin, and I don't see a lot of bleed through. The graph printing is not too light or dark, and it's just what I would expect from a spiral notebook. The pages are perforated and tear out easily and cleanly.My two older kids use them for math class, and this 'bulk' set keeps me happy, since I have spares ready to go.

K

Kenny T.

Dark grid lines make it hard to read notes in pencil!

I really wish I hadn't bought the pack and only bought 1 notebook to try out. Next time I'm following my intuition. The blue lines for the grid are too darkly colored so that I don't want to write in pencil in my notebook because the dark grid lines make it hard to read. So now I use ink, and since ink bleeds through often, making it even harder to read my notes, I only use one sides of pages instead of 2. Not buying this again. Maybe it works for others but next time, make sure to include a picture of the inside!

123
